item.text:
**3B.1 Research Note: Fumio Kishida (2024)**

**Bottom line:** The 2024 record is mixed but leans positive on this lens. Kishida made explicit, public moves to acknowledge and remedy a major past state abuse case, and he repeatedly framed human rights, inclusion, and rule of law as government commitments. The main negative evidence is structural: Japan’s criminal-justice system still drew credible criticism in 2024 for “hostage justice,” coercive interrogation, harsh pretrial detention, and the death penalty, with the Hakamada acquittal underscoring the risk of arbitrary punishment. I did not find 2024 evidence of Kishida ordering or endorsing torture, disappearances, political imprisonment, or extrajudicial killing.

- [Video Message by Prime Minister Kishida at the Symposium on Inclusive Society and Human Rights](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202402/05_message.html)  
  - **Publisher:** Prime Minister’s Office of Japan  
  - **Date:** February 5, 2024  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Kishida said Japan must not tolerate discriminatory treatment or violence against minorities, explicitly tied government policy to the rule of law, fundamental human rights, and “human dignity,” and urged steady efforts toward an inclusive society.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.1

- [Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida Regarding the Ruling on a Lawsuit over the Former Eugenics Protection Law and Other Matters](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/03kaiken.html)  
  - **Publisher:** Prime Minister’s Office of Japan  
  - **Date:** July 3, 2024  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Kishida said the former Eugenics Protection Law was unconstitutional, expressed “sincere remorse” and “profound apology,” promised swift compensation, and instructed ministers to develop new guarantees after recognizing the state’s liability for past forced sterilizations.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.1

- [Kishida apologizes to victims of forced sterilization](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2024/07/17/japan/society/kishida-eugenics-victims/)  
  - **Publisher:** The Japan Times  
  - **Date:** July 17, 2024  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Kishida apologized in person to more than 100 forced-sterilization victims and said the government would move quickly on a new compensation framework, which is direct accountability for a past state human-rights abuse.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.1

- [World Report 2024: Japan](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/japan)  
  - **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch  
  - **Date:** 2024  
  - **Claim-level summary:** HRW said Japan’s “hostage justice” system coerces confessions through repeated arrests, denial of bail, and uncounseled questioning; it also flagged death-row secrecy and criticized the continued use of capital punishment.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.1

- [Japan’s Abusive ‘Hostage Justice’ System Persists](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/01/japans-abusive-hostage-justice-system-persists)  
  - **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch  
  - **Date:** October 1, 2024  
  - **Claim-level summary:** HRW said abusive pretrial detention and coerced confessions were still ongoing in Japan, and used the Hakamada case to illustrate wrongful conviction and the persistence of arbitrary punishment.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.1

- [Japanese man acquitted of 1966 murders after 45 years on death row](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/japanese-man-acquitted-of-1966-murders-after-45-years-on-death-row-3633320)  
  - **Publisher:** Reuters  
  - **Date:** September 26, 2024  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Reuters reported Iwao Hakamada’s acquittal after 45 years on death row, a stark sign that Japan’s justice system had still produced an extreme wrongful-punishment case during Kishida’s term.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.1

**Search gap:** I found no 2024 evidence that Kishida directly confronted torture, disappearances, political imprisonment, or extrajudicial killing in Japan, and no evidence that his government used those tools. The clearest adverse evidence is instead structural criminal-justice abuse and the death-penalty system, not a documented campaign of state terror.
